### Earlier roles (1990–2004)
In 2002, Silva starred opposite Bimbo Akintola in _Keeping Faith_. Akintola later cited Silva, whom she refers to as "Aunty Joke", as a major career influence, adding, "Silva has done a lot, but it's not even about the things that she did, it's about the things she didn't realize that she did".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-15) Also in 2002, Silva co-produced and starred in _The Kingmaker_ with Olu Jacobs.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFoubiri2015351-16) This was followed by roles in pictures such as _A Husband's Wife_ (2003), _Shylock_ (2004), and _A Past Came Calling_ (2004).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-lap-17)

### Critical success (2006–present)
[edit]
In 2006, Silva was awarded the "Best Actress in a Leading Role" award at the 2nd Africa Movie Academy Awards for her role in _Women's Cot_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-19) Later that year, Silva starred opposite Genevieve Nnaji in Mildred Okwo's action thriller _30 Days_, which received 10 nominations at the Africa Movie Academy Awards in 2008.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-21) She also narrated Jeta Amata's Anglo-Nigerian production _The Amazing Grace_,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaynes2016325-22) which was shot in Calabar.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-tn-23) The film was lauded by critics and was nominated for 11 Africa Movie Academy Awards.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-24)_The News_ noted Silva's "song-like voice, [which] provides insight to the actions".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-tn-23)

### Critical success (2006–present)
In 2007, Silva starred opposite Kate Henshaw-Nuttal, Michael Okon, and Fred Essien in Ndubuisi Okoh's _To Love and to Hold_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-25) Silva won a Best Supporting Actress award in 2008[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-allafrica1-26) for her "methodical portrayal of a grandmother" in _White Waters_ (2007), though she was not at the ceremony to receive her award in person.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-27) In a November 2008 interview, Silva professed that "whenever she had to play an evil character in a film, she would pray and use Jesus as her 'hedge'".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBender2012112-28) Silva is also the recipient of an EMOTAN Award from African Independent Television (AIT) and the SOLIDRA Award for Visual Art.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-IN-8)

### Critical success (2006–present)
In 2011, Silva starred alongside Nse Ikpe Etim, Wale Ojo, and Lydia Forson in Kunle Afolayan's romantic comedy _Phone Swap_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-29) Lauded by the critics, and one of the most eagerly awaited films of the year,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-30) it received four nominations at the 8th Africa Movie Academy Awards, including a nomination for Best Nigerian Film. It also won the award for Achievement in Productions Design.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-AMAA-31) In 2013, Silva took to the stage to appear in the Thespian Family Theatre and Productions staging of the "Mad King of Ijudiya" at the Agip Hall of Muson Centre of Lagos at Christmas. Two shows were put up at 3:00 pm and 6:00 pm on 21, 22, 28, and 29 December, which _Vanguard_ described as a "rich blend of folklore, traditional dance, and music that naturally transports the audience to a typical African village setting".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-32)

## United Nations Goodwill Ambassador
[edit]
In October 2012, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime appointed Silva as goodwill ambassador. In accordance with the UN policy of enlisting prominent figures in art, music, film, sport, and literature to assist with their campaigns, her role was focused on her participation in the fight against human trafficking in Nigeria. Work fighting human trafficking was part of the "I Am Priceless" campaign, which had also received support from the Nigerian authorities. Silva's appointment was for a period of three years.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-34)
Silva was married to veteran actor Olu Jacobs and has two children. The couple met in 1981 at the National Theatre, Lagos during the 21st Independence anniversary.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-naij10-12)
Silva is director of studies at the Lufodo Academy of Performing Arts, while her husband served as chairman.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-lap-17) Lufodo Academy is one of several assets the couple owns as part of the Lufodo Group, including Lufodo Productions, Lufodo Consult, and Lufodo Distribution. She has curated for the Bank of Industry (BOI) in Theatre, Film, Documentary and Poetry and the 2012 London Olympics,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-IN-8) and is also the pioneer managing director of Malete Film Village, in association with Kwara State University.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-CN-11)
In addition to her work as an actress, Silva is a philanthropist and a strong supporter of women's emancipation and empowerment, contributing to their education, training, and progress.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-AKA2012-35)

### Earlier roles (1990–2004)
In 2002, Silva starred opposite Bimbo Akintola in _Keeping Faith_. Akintola later cited Silva, whom she refers to as "Aunty Joke", as a major career influence, adding, "Silva has done a lot, but it's not even about the things that she did, it's about the things she didn't realize that she did".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-15) Also in 2002, Silva co-produced and starred in _The Kingmaker_ with Olu Jacobs.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFoubiri2015351-16) This was followed by roles in pictures such as _A Husband's Wife_ (2003), _Shylock_ (2004), and _A Past Came Calling_ (2004).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-lap-17)

### Critical success (2006–present)
[edit]
In 2006, Silva was awarded the "Best Actress in a Leading Role" award at the 2nd Africa Movie Academy Awards for her role in _Women's Cot_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-19) Later that year, Silva starred opposite Genevieve Nnaji in Mildred Okwo's action thriller _30 Days_, which received 10 nominations at the Africa Movie Academy Awards in 2008.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-21) She also narrated Jeta Amata's Anglo-Nigerian production _The Amazing Grace_,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaynes2016325-22) which was shot in Calabar.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-tn-23) The film was lauded by critics and was nominated for 11 Africa Movie Academy Awards.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-24)_The News_ noted Silva's "song-like voice, [which] provides insight to the actions".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-tn-23)

### Critical success (2006–present)
In 2007, Silva starred opposite Kate Henshaw-Nuttal, Michael Okon, and Fred Essien in Ndubuisi Okoh's _To Love and to Hold_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-25) Silva won a Best Supporting Actress award in 2008[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-allafrica1-26) for her "methodical portrayal of a grandmother" in _White Waters_ (2007), though she was not at the ceremony to receive her award in person.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-27) In a November 2008 interview, Silva professed that "whenever she had to play an evil character in a film, she would pray and use Jesus as her 'hedge'".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBender2012112-28) Silva is also the recipient of an EMOTAN Award from African Independent Television (AIT) and the SOLIDRA Award for Visual Art.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-IN-8)

### Critical success (2006–present)
In 2011, Silva starred alongside Nse Ikpe Etim, Wale Ojo, and Lydia Forson in Kunle Afolayan's romantic comedy _Phone Swap_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-29) Lauded by the critics, and one of the most eagerly awaited films of the year,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-30) it received four nominations at the 8th Africa Movie Academy Awards, including a nomination for Best Nigerian Film. It also won the award for Achievement in Productions Design.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-AMAA-31) In 2013, Silva took to the stage to appear in the Thespian Family Theatre and Productions staging of the "Mad King of Ijudiya" at the Agip Hall of Muson Centre of Lagos at Christmas. Two shows were put up at 3:00 pm and 6:00 pm on 21, 22, 28, and 29 December, which _Vanguard_ described as a "rich blend of folklore, traditional dance, and music that naturally transports the audience to a typical African village setting".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-32)

## United Nations Goodwill Ambassador
[edit]
In October 2012, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime appointed Silva as goodwill ambassador. In accordance with the UN policy of enlisting prominent figures in art, music, film, sport, and literature to assist with their campaigns, her role was focused on her participation in the fight against human trafficking in Nigeria. Work fighting human trafficking was part of the "I Am Priceless" campaign, which had also received support from the Nigerian authorities. Silva's appointment was for a period of three years.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-34)
Silva was married to veteran actor Olu Jacobs and has two children. The couple met in 1981 at the National Theatre, Lagos during the 21st Independence anniversary.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-naij10-12)
Silva is director of studies at the Lufodo Academy of Performing Arts, while her husband served as chairman.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-lap-17) Lufodo Academy is one of several assets the couple owns as part of the Lufodo Group, including Lufodo Productions, Lufodo Consult, and Lufodo Distribution. She has curated for the Bank of Industry (BOI) in Theatre, Film, Documentary and Poetry and the 2012 London Olympics,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-IN-8) and is also the pioneer managing director of Malete Film Village, in association with Kwara State University.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-CN-11)
In addition to her work as an actress, Silva is a philanthropist and a strong supporter of women's emancipation and empowerment, contributing to their education, training, and progress.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joke_Silva#cite_note-AKA2012-35)
